name: loihi2_like
display_name: Intel Loihi 2 (Intel 4, Intel technology brief 2021): 128 cores, dense equivalent 128 x 1024

faithfulness.note: Geometry only: the registered geometry resolves with its claim class (curve-only), and no physics profile ships for this target (the brief states no per-event energy or step time), so absolute area, energy and latency are refused by name.

notes: A vendor technology brief (Intel Corporation, 'Taking Neuromorphic Computing to the Next Level with Loihi 2', 2021, footer code 0921/SBAI/KC/PDF; not peer reviewed). The registered geometry is the dense equivalent of the per-core synaptic memory at 8-bit weights, the loihi bundle's rule: "Up to 128 KB synaptic memory" over 1024 of the stated "Up to 8192 neurons" (Figure 1, p.5) gives 128 axons, on "Max # Neuron Cores/Chip 128" (Table 2, p.7). Fan-in and weight precision are not stated, and the brief credits Loihi 2's capacity to compression and flexible partitioning ("192 KB, flexible allocation", Table 2), which a dense core cannot represent: curve-only. The chip's permissions, were a physics form declared: a core implements "a group of spiking neurons, including all synapses connecting to the neurons" (p.5), so no inter-core partial sum (no coalescing), and Table 2 lists "Core fan-out list compression and sharing" (p.7), so a source reaches several cores (neuron splitting).
